text:
sam: prod alert - saw 2 OOMs on us-west-inference-2 for model redwood/longgen-v1 around 15:30 UTC. GPU memory spiked to 95% then OOM. tagging @eng-runtime and @oncall. logs attached (stack traces + allocator dumps).
anna: looking. timeline shows a kernel-selector change rolled 3h ago (v0.9.3) that prefers fused attention for >2k tokens. suspect workspace size growth.
raj: confirmed on staging. profiler (nvprof + internal) shows max_workspace_bytes jumped ~25% for the attention kernel at seq_len=4096. also noticed batching heuristic started coalescing more long sequences into same batch.
maria: kv cache behavior also changed after the rollout — eviction seemed delayed which increased per-request peak memory. probably two orthogonal regressions that amplify each other.
sam: quick triage plan: 1) disable kernel auto-reroute -> force previous kernel 2) tighten batching heuristic for long sequences 3) set temporary kvcache eviction threshold 4) enable circuit breaker to reject huge requests. Who can patch canary?
anna: I can patch kernel selector to pin to kernel_id: "attn_v0.9.2_fallback" on canary. small change in kernel_registry config. Command:

```
# canary config patch
kubectl -n inference set env deploy/runner KERNEL_SELECTOR_OVERRIDE=attn_v0.9.2_fallback
```

raj: I'll add a quick guard in batching: if median_seq_len > 1024 and batch_size_estimated_tokens > 4096 -> split batch. Patch as runtime flag: BATCHING_MAX_TOKENS_PER_BATCH=4096

maria: KV cache temp policy:

```
# env overrides for canary
KVCACHE_EVICT_PERCENT=30  # aggressive
KVCACHE_MAX_ITEMS=200000
```

sam: also propose a short circuit-breaker rule to reject requests with seq_len > 8192 and prompt_tokens > 120k for the next 2h, with 503 + Retry-After.
oncall-bot: paging sam, anna, raj (oncall). Incident created: INC-2025-1789
anna: deploying kernel pin to canary now.
deploy-bot: canary deploy started: inference-runner-canary (image: runner:2026-03-17-rc4)
raj: batching patch uploaded to PR #4127, adding unit test and perf test. Will run perf harness on canary.
maria: kvcache changes applied to canary, monitoring eviction rate. initial telemetry shows per-GPU mem peak down ~18%.
sam: good. after canary stabilizes, plan to backport quick fixes to prod with 30m staged rollout and monitor OOM rate.
anna: note — we should also add a workspace hard cap env: REDWOOD_WORKSPACE_MAX_BYTES=6_000_000_000 (6GB) for now. This forces kernel to allocate smaller temp buffers or fallback to a slower kernel path.
raj: added perf note — forcing smaller workspace will increase latency for some long requests ~10-15% but prevents OOM cascade. acceptable trade for incident window.
maria: logs from canary show fewer OOM traces; KV eviction increased as expected. Adding dashboard widget to track: gpu_mem_peak, kvcache_hit_rate, batch_tokens_distribution.
sam: action items (short):
- anna: kernel selector pin + rollback PR
- raj: batching heuristic change + perf tests
- maria: kvcache eviction tuning + dashboard
- sam: circuit-breaker rule + prod rollout plan

anna: PR opened to revert kernel-selector default (draft) and patch to set KERNEL_SELECTOR_OVERRIDE via rollout config.
deploy-bot: canary deploy succeeded. health checks OK. monitoring: reduced OOM alerts.
oncall-bot: scheduled follow-up at +1h for incident review.
sam: once prod rollback is approved we'll do a staged rollback to v0.9.2 selector, then run a controlled experiment to reintroduce fused attention with workspace safeguards and a perf regression ticket.
raj: adding regression test to CI that asserts workspace_bytes <= baseline * 1.1 for seq_len in [512,1024,4096].
maria: saving allocator dumps from the incident for postmortem. tagging for perf regression: PERF-1724.
sam: thanks team. will update incident channel with timeline and postmortem link after follow-up. :thumbsup:
